hotel.name: Business hotel, Shinjuku west exit
hotel.valueWhy: Small rooms but immaculate, and the transit access saves real time every single day of a busy itinerary.

hotel.name: Capsule-style private room, Shinjuku
hotel.valueWhy: Cheapest option in the area, but genuinely tight for two people and bags — fine for a short stay only.

hotel.name: Design hotel, Shimokitazawa
hotel.valueWhy: Above budget, but a genuinely spacious room and puts you inside the neighborhood you're already planning to explore.

hotel.name: Standard hotel, Asakusa
hotel.valueWhy: Solid value, but further from your Oct 14–18 focus neighborhoods than Shinjuku — more transit time daily.

hotel.name: Business hotel, Kiyosumi-Shirakawa
hotel.valueWhy: Quiet, coffee-shop-dense area with easy access to the Oct 14 plan, but a longer ride out to Hakone/Nikko mornings.

hotel.name: Boutique hotel, Daikanyama
hotel.valueWhy: Beautiful and well over budget for what you get — the design premium outweighs the room itself.

hostel.name: Social hostel, Asakusa
hostel.valueWhy: Lively common area without being loud late, and Asakusa is the most hostel-dense, budget-friendly base in the city.

hostel.name: Quiet hostel, Kiyosumi-Shirakawa
hostel.valueWhy: Calm, coffee-shop neighborhood — good for early Hakone/Nikko mornings, but a smaller common area with less social pull.

hostel.name: Party-leaning hostel, Shibuya
hostel.valueWhy: Cheapest on paper, but reviews consistently flag noise well past your stated quiet-hours preference.

hostel.name: Capsule hostel, Shinjuku
hostel.valueWhy: Very private for a hostel (individual capsules), but that also means almost no common-area social scene.

hostel.name: Family-run guesthouse, Yanaka
hostel.valueWhy: Charming and quiet, but the transit walk is longer than the other options and it's a smaller, less social property.

hostel.name: Modern hostel, Ueno
hostel.valueWhy: Good common-kitchen social scene and strong transit access, slightly further from the Oct 14–17 neighborhoods.

hotel.name: Business hotel, Nagano Station
hotel.valueWhy: Simple and small, but you're only here one night — proximity to the Shinkansen matters more than room size.

hotel.name: Ryokan-style inn, Zenkoji approach
hotel.valueWhy: Lovely traditional feel next to Nakamise-dori, but the temple-adjacent premium is steep for a single night.

hotel.name: Standard hotel, Nagano Station east
hotel.valueWhy: Best price-to-location ratio for a one-night stopover before Kyoto.

hotel.name: Mid-range hotel, Zenkoji-dori
hotel.valueWhy: Comfortable middle ground, but no real advantage over the station-front options for one night.

hostel.name: Small guesthouse, Zenkoji area
hostel.valueWhy: Cheap and characterful, but Nagano's hostel scene is thin — expect a quiet, low-social single night.

hotel.name: Business hotel, Kiyamachi
hotel.valueWhy: Right in the nightlife strip you planned for, small rooms but excellent walkability to everything on your Kyoto days.

hotel.name: Modern hotel, Kyoto Station
hotel.valueWhy: Unmatched transit hub access for day trips to Uji/Ohara/Kurama, but October foliage pricing pushes it near the top of budget.

hotel.name: Machiya-style inn, Gion edge
hotel.valueWhy: Beautiful traditional character, but this one runs over your stated budget for what's a fairly compact room.

hotel.name: Standard hotel, Karasuma
hotel.valueWhy: Solid, unremarkable, and a 12-minute walk to Kiyamachi's evening scene — good value if you don't mind the extra walk.

hotel.name: Budget hotel, Shijo-Omiya
hotel.valueWhy: Best price in the sample, on a quieter street one stop from Kiyamachi by tram.

hotel.name: Boutique hotel, Pontocho
hotel.valueWhy: Gorgeous river-alley location, but well past budget for four nights — better as a one-night splurge than the whole stay.

hostel.name: Social hostel, Kawaramachi
hostel.valueWhy: Right by Kiyamachi's bars, active common area, and the walk-in cost is under half the hotel options nearby.

hostel.name: Traditional-style hostel, Gion
hostel.valueWhy: Nice atmosphere but reviews mention thin walls — a real trade-off against your quiet-hours preference.

hotel.name: Business hotel, Kurashiki Station
hotel.valueWhy: Simple, well-located for a one-night stop, and cheap relative to everywhere else on this trip.

hotel.name: Canal-view inn, Bikan district
hotel.valueWhy: The willow-lined canal view is genuinely special, but it's a big price jump for one night and a longer walk to the station.

hotel.name: Standard hotel, Kurashiki south exit
hotel.valueWhy: Cheapest reasonable option, slightly further from the Bikan district than the station-front pick.

hostel.name: Small guesthouse, near Bikan district
hostel.valueWhy: Good value and closer to the canal district for evening photos, but a modest, low-key common area.

hotel.name: Business hotel, Hakata Station
hotel.valueWhy: Right on the Shinkansen/airport line, and Fukuoka runs noticeably cheaper than Tokyo/Kyoto for the same tier.

hotel.name: Standard hotel, Nakasu
hotel.valueWhy: Steps from the yatai stalls for your planned nights out — you'll walk home in under 5 minutes.

hotel.name: Budget hotel, Tenjin
hotel.valueWhy: Cheapest of the group, a 10–12 minute walk to Nakasu instead of right on top of it.

hostel.name: Social hostel, Hakata
hostel.valueWhy: Well-reviewed common kitchen/lounge, quiet-hours enforced after 10pm — matches what you asked for closely.

hostel.name: Riverside hostel, Nakasu
hostel.valueWhy: Great location for the yatai scene, but reviews note it can run loud on weekend nights.

hostel.name: Guesthouse, Tenjin
hostel.valueWhy: Cheapest option here with a genuinely social common room, just a bit further from the water.

hotel.name: Business hotel, Nagasaki Station
hotel.valueWhy: Central to Dejima and the tram network, straightforward and reliable for a one-night stop.

hotel.name: Hillside hotel, Mt. Inasa side
hotel.valueWhy: Harbor views worth the small premium if you're already going up for the night view — otherwise skip it.

hostel.name: Social hostel, Nagasaki Station area
hostel.valueWhy: Good common area, close to the tram line you'll use for Dejima and Chinatown the next morning.

hotel.name: Onsen ryokan, Unzen Onsen town
hotel.valueWhy: Over your usual budget, but the free-text override case — a real onsen ryokan experience in the town built around exactly that.

hotel.name: Simple inn, Unzen jigoku area
hotel.valueWhy: Right by the geothermal walk, plainer room, no included dinner — best if you want to keep to budget here.

hostel.name: Small guesthouse, Unzen Onsen
hostel.valueWhy: Cheapest option in a small onsen town — thin hostel selection here, so expect a quiet, low-social night either way.
